items.text: The Trump–Putin–Xi trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen is now confirmed by all three governments. Trump's newly released schedule puts it at the Kylin Villa resort at 2:30 p.m. local time on Nov 19, and China's Foreign Ministry confirmed it on Monday. The Kremlin announced it on Nov 14. DPA reports that a US official called it a first step, played down expectations, and said Trump wants to discuss cutting nuclear arsenals after New START expired.
items.notes: Updates E-261115-05, which said the trilateral was unconfirmed. Kremlin announcement Nov 14 (https://tass.com/politics/2218203); Chinese MFA confirmation (https://tass.com/world/2218433). TASS is Russian state media, but the White House schedule confirmation is backed by DPA. On Face the Nation, Rep. Moolenaar said he does not expect any agreements.

items.text: Transportation Secretary Duffy said on the Sunday shows that the Nov 13 nationwide ground stop most likely traced to a router or its installation. Maintenance in El Dorado, Arkansas, triggered a system L3Harris had installed weeks earlier in Amarillo, Texas, which flooded the FAA network. The router is being tested at an L3Harris lab in Florida with the FBI offering help. Duffy and FAA chief Bedford say there is no sign of a cyberattack, though the root cause is not final. About 2,300 flights were still cancelled on Sunday. Trump blamed the Biden administration, and Rep. Himes argued the FAA should first spend the $12.5 billion already approved before Congress considers Duffy's $50 billion request.
items.reporter: Ivan Pereira, Ayesha Ali, Clara McMichael (ABC)
items.outlet: US Department of Transportation; ABC News
items.notes: Follows E-261114-08. Duffy says the affected routers date from 2001. United CEO Kirby called it a call to action. Himes remarks from the Face the Nation transcript: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/face-the-nation-full-transcript-11-15-2026/

items.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said six drones targeted a US air-defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain on Sunday, in retaliation for unspecified US actions. Bahrain said it intercepted missiles and drones, its first such interception since September, and told residents to take shelter. Reuters reported no immediate US or Bahraini confirmation of any hit. The attack comes a day after Reuters reported that Trump may hold off new strikes unless Iran provokes.
items.notes: No CENTCOM statement found for Nov 15. An AA briefing also cited an IRGC claim of downing a US MQ-1 over Qeshm, but a similar claim was dated Nov 6 (Shafaq), so it was left out as unverified/possibly old. Nothing new found on Vance–Rezaei.

items.text: House China Select Committee chair John Moolenaar said on CBS's Face the Nation that Nvidia's Jensen Huang has agreed to a closed-door interview with the committee, with dates still being set. Moolenaar said Huang had severely compromised national security and wants chip export controls written into the NDAA. Rep. Jim Himes said it is unknown whether the employee at the centre of the affair was a Chinese intelligence asset and called for scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Lutnick.
items.notes: Relevant to W-261113-02 (Huang testimony); a closed-door interview is not the same as public testimony, so the watch item stays open.

items.text: Senate HELP chair Bill Cassidy said on Face the Nation that the US has lost its measles-elimination status and accused HHS Secretary Kennedy of covering for failures on measles, food policy and costs. Kennedy had said the Senate no longer has leverage over him. PAHO has still not commented officially. Forbes, citing KFF Health News, says the decision is expected to be announced on Nov 17. CDC counts 5,412 cases in 2026, and states report 10 deaths against the CDC's six.
items.notes: Follows E-261115-01. W-261115-01 remains open because there is still no official PAHO/CDC statement. Cassidy is undecided on FDA nominee Heidi Overton, whose vote he said is Wednesday.

items.text: US District Judge Ana Reyes temporarily barred the administration from closing East Potomac Park and its public golf course in Washington for a planned redevelopment. She issued the order on Saturday, a day before the planned 15-month closure, and it runs through Nov 28. She cited Trump's own posts as evidence the plan was final, questioned the government's safety rationale, and plans to name former US attorney Jessie Liu as special master to examine whether officials misled the court. DOJ, which has asked Reyes to step aside, vowed to defend the plan, and Trump attacked the judge.
items.notes: The ruling came Saturday Nov 14, possibly just before the previous window, but it was not logged in events/2026-11-14 or 11-15.

items.text: Red 'Slava UPA' graffiti found on Saturday on two Warsaw monuments, the Ghetto Heroes Monument and the 1st Polish Army Soldier monument, adds to a series of about a dozen similar incidents in Poznań, Gdańsk and Gdynia. On Sunday Warsaw Mayor Trzaskowski said the scale points to a possible organised provocation; the Ukrainian embassy and the special-services spokesman blamed Russian hybrid operations that pay young Ukrainians, and a 17-year-old Ukrainian has been charged in Gdańsk. Warsaw police have made no arrests; the Jewish Historical Institute condemned the attacks.
items.notes: Warsaw graffiti found Nov 14 morning (TVN24 Warszawa: https://tvn24.pl/tvnwarszawa/srodmiescie/napisy-dotyczace-ukrainy-na-pomnikach-w-warszawie-st9338937); not logged earlier. Trzaskowski reaction and NfP roundup are Nov 15. Attribution to Russia is a claim by the government spokesman and the Ukrainian embassy. Reports differ on where the teenager was detained (Gdańsk per NfP, Gdynia per TVN24).

items.text: Payment processor Autopay disclosed that attackers gained unauthorised access to part of its infrastructure and some payment-related data, an incident it detected on Nov 11. The company says the largely automated, AI-assisted attack used no malware or phishing, transaction processing was not affected, and it cannot rule out data copying; it has notified UODO, the police and CSIRT KNF and is contacting affected customers. It has not said how many people are affected.
items.notes: Details are the company's own account (spokesperson Zuzanna Szybisty). No independent confirmation of scale.

items.text: The appointments of Andrzej Domański as deputy PM and Agnieszka Bartol as funds and regional policy minister remain unsigned almost four weeks on. The President's Chancellery said on Sunday the ceremony will happen once a suitable slot in the calendar is found, but gave no date; presidential adviser Błażej Poboży said the President would not block it. KO politicians blamed the President for the delay.
items.notes: No change to watch W-261105-07 (still open). The article does not mention the NBP board appointments.

items.text: Truck queues at the Ukrainian border reached about 42 km (about 330 trucks) at Hrebenne and 16 km (about 650 trucks) at Dorohusk on Sunday, with waits of roughly 26 to 30 hours. Officials blame heavier pre-year-end freight traffic and expect queues could last until the third week of December; they say renovation work at both crossings does not slow processing.
items.notes: Single outlet read.

items.text: Bucharest gendarmerie said 105 people, 100 of them Polish citizens, were taken to police stations after clashes following Romania's 2–1 Nations League win over Poland on Saturday. Proceedings were opened against 74 people for violently resisting officers, and one faces pyrotechnics charges; one Pole reportedly went to hospital.
items.notes: Match on Nov 14; figures announced Nov 15. No Polish MFA statement found.

items.text: The Left hosted a Party of European Socialists meeting, 'No Step Back! Progressive Mobilisation', in Wrocław. Speakers including MEP Krzysztof Śmiszek, Labour Minister Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk and Senate deputy speaker Magdalena Biejat attacked the radical right and President Nawrocki's veto of the online child-protection measures, and called for taxes on big digital firms and excess profits.
items.notes: No formal decisions taken.

items.text: Mayor Łukasz Gibała has signed orders sending the City Council draft resolutions to take Kraków out of several associations, among them EUROCITIES, the Małopolska Tourist Organisation, the Kraków Tourism Alliance (Organizacja Turystyczna Stołecznego Królewskiego Miasta Krakowa), City Destinations Alliance and the Association of Małopolska Municipalities and Counties. He puts the savings at about 8.2m zł a year; in 2026 the city paid 5.6m zł to the Kraków tourism body and 2.27m zł to the Małopolska one. The BIP agenda for the 18 Nov session lists nine withdrawal resolutions (druki 1628-1636) for a single reading. That is one more than the eight named by LoveKraków: the European Coalition of Cities Against Racism.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Updates open watch W-261105-08 (checkDate Nov 25): the vote is now scheduled for the 18 Nov session. LoveKraków lists 8 bodies; BIP lists 9 druki.

items.text: Małopolska Police said on X that the 141 officers sent to Warsaw on the day of the 7 Nov Main Square attack came from the Kraków Police Prevention Unit (OPP, more than 500 officers), not from the Kraków city command. According to the police, 128 prevention officers were on duty in Kraków under the city command that day, plus operational officers. The police were responding to claims by opposition politicians and some media that sending officers to guard the Constitutional Tribunal weakened security in Kraków.
items.notes: Police statement relayed by PAP. The opposition's version (officers diverted to the Constitutional Tribunal) is not independently checked here.

items.text: A hiker was swept away and buried by an avalanche near Żółta Turnia in the Polish Tatras on Sunday afternoon. TOPR rescuers recovered his body about 30 cm under the snow; LoveKraków calls it Poland's first avalanche death of the 2026/27 season. Earlier that day a 25-year-old Pole died after falling about 100 m on Gerlach in the Slovak Tatras, according to Slovak mountain rescue (HZS). TOPR advises against going into high terrain, where trails are unbroken and icy after fresh snow.
items.notes: Małopolska (Tatras), not Kraków city. Facts from TOPR and HZS as relayed by LoveKraków. The article gives no avalanche danger level.

items.text: 178 firefighters with 47 vehicles fought a fire for about 15.5 hours at a building in Giebułtów (Kraków county) that housed a car workshop, a paint shop and part of a home. The fire was reported at 20:29 on Saturday and put out at 12:04 on Sunday. The one occupant got out unhurt; a volunteer firefighter was slightly hurt when two fire engines collided on icy roads. The hydrant network could not keep up, so crews brought water in by tanker relay (about 500,000 litres). Building inspectors will assess whether the building can still be used.
items.notes: Figures from the Kraków fire service (KM PSP) spokesman Maciej Podymkiewicz.

items.text: The city of Kraków says it has received over 5.3m zł after the Court of Appeal in Kraków on 26 Oct upheld a 2023 judgment against the liquidator of the former Dr A. Wander SA. The State Treasury, represented by the mayor, had sued over proceeds from the 2014 sale of the company's building at ul. Św. Krzyża 17, which had been moved to Switzerland. The 2023 award was about 6.42m zł plus interest; part went on costs.

MPK Kraków chose Italy's MECNO SERVICE, the only bidder after a competitive dialogue, to supply a rail-grinding machine for tram tracks for over 12m zł gross. Grinding is meant to cut noise and vibration and slow rail wear. The contract is due to be signed in 2026, and the machine should be in service by mid-2028.

Małopolska Voivode Krzysztof Klęczar signed an annex releasing a further 2.5m zł of central-government money for the Niepołomice bypass, the last of three 2026 instalments (over 5.6m zł this year). The project costs over 74m zł. Completion is now planned for 2027; the headline says a deadline was missed, but the article does not say which one.
items.notes: Małopolska (Wieliczka county).

items.text: The Bay of Bengal system strengthened into a deep depression on Monday morning (Nov 16), about 870 km SSE of Visakhapatnam and 980 km SSE of Gopalpur, moving north-northwest. IMD expects it to become Cyclone Akvan by Monday evening, a severe cyclonic storm on Nov 17 and a very severe cyclonic storm by Nov 19, heading toward the Andhra Pradesh coast; IMD has not yet given an official landfall point. An IMD scientist told Deccan Chronicle it could cross the coast between Visakhapatnam and Bapatla around Nov 20. Odisha has issued yellow and orange rain alerts for Nov 18–21 and readied disaster-response forces.
items.notes: Follows E-261114-41 and the Nov 15 depression event. Not yet officially a cyclonic storm as of the window close; IMD bulletin PDF not opened directly. The Vizag–Bapatla landfall comes from one IMD scientist (Dr S. Karunasagar) via Deccan Chronicle, not an official IMD forecast. Daily Jagran (Nov 16) adds very heavy rain in Chennai and nearby districts on Nov 18–19. Watch W-261111-03 stays open.

items.text: PM Modi left for Manila on Nov 16 for the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, which the Philippines hosts on Nov 17. In his departure statement he called ASEAN central to India's Act East Policy and MAHASAGAR vision. Separately, Philippine Defence Secretary Teodoro said Manila wants more BrahMos missile units and has sent India a wish list. India is also pushing a review of the ASEAN–India goods trade agreement (AITIGA), which MEA says will take time.
items.notes: Departure statement carried by PTI (Business Standard). The BrahMos wish list and AITIGA details come from the ANI report in The Tribune, Nov 15: https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/world/us-state-dept-slams-report-claiming-trump-admin-ignoring-quad-says-manila-meet-will-formalise-leaders-summit

items.text: Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah launched the cooperative ride-hailing service Bharat Taxi in Maharashtra, in Pune, on Nov 15. It runs through Sahakar Taxi Cooperative, a multi-state cooperative in which drivers ('Sarathis') are member-owners and pay no commission. Officials said about 10 lakh drivers have registered nationally and about 32,000 in Pune, with 60 lakh customers and about 20,000 rides a day.
items.notes: Registration figures come from MoS Murlidhar Mohol and Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar (claims). This is a competitor to Ola and Uber. Shah's Pune visit continues Nov 16.

items.text: On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas (Birsa Munda's birth anniversary), PM Modi joined a Gadchiroli, Maharashtra event by video and launched 246 tribal-welfare projects worth about ₹3,000 crore, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools and 100 PM-JANMAN multipurpose centres. Modi claimed India had freed itself from Naxalism-Maoism, saying about 125 districts had been affected in 2014.
items.notes: Organiser is RSS-affiliated, so the project list was cross-checked with the News24 Hindi liveblog (246 projects, ₹3,000 cr). The 'Maoism-free' line is Modi's claim; no independent verification.

items.text: UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched distribution of another 25 lakh free tablets to students in Lucknow under the Swami Vivekananda Yuva Sashaktikaran Yojana, with ₹2,374.6 crore earmarked in the state budget. The scheme has no income or age limit, and the state says total beneficiaries will reach about 85 lakh. The launch comes ahead of the 2027 UP assembly election, and Adityanath used it to attack the previous SP government.
items.notes: No opposition response found.

items.text: Delhi's air improved after light western-disturbance rain, with the city average AQI at 218 ('poor') at 8 am on Nov 16, down from about 350 ('very poor') on Sunday morning, according to CPCB data. The early-warning system expects the air to worsen again to 'very poor' on Nov 17–18 as winds weaken, and IMD forecasts no rain from Nov 16 to 20.
items.notes: GRAP status not stated in the article (Stage III in force since Nov 6, per earlier events). The SC hearing in the pollution case (W-261106-13) is due later on Nov 16, after this window.

items.text: The US State Department rejected a Politico report that the Quad was struggling under the Trump administration. Assistant Secretary Dylan Johnson called it ridiculous and said Washington is working to formalise a Quad Leaders' Summit at the ASEAN meetings in Manila. India's MEA again would not confirm a Quad leaders' meeting or a Modi–Trump meeting as Modi left for Manila on Nov 16.
items.notes: Follows E-261114-53 and the Nov 15 event. Watch W-261113-13 resolves on Nov 17.

items.text: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, speaking in Cairo, said India and the US have already agreed that Indian goods will get preferential access to the US market, with lower duties than competitor countries, settled when Modi and Trump announced the framework. An unnamed Indian official told PTI the aim is now to close the first tranche by the end of this financial year (March 2027). There was no on-record US confirmation.
items.notes: Goyal's on-record version of the Nov 13 Bloomberg/government-sources item (logged Nov 14). The end-FY target suggests the deal may not be signed by the Dec G20 that W-261026-28 expects; that watch stays open.

items.text: In a filing reported over the weekend, US prosecutors asked Judge Victor Marrero to sentence Nikhil Gupta to 293 months (about 24 years) for the plot to murder Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. That is the top of the guidelines range, and prosecutors say a co-conspirator was an Indian government employee. Gupta's lawyers asked for 12 years, in line with the probation recommendation, and in a letter Gupta apologised and cited alcohol dependence. Sentencing is set for Nov 20; India denies involvement.
items.notes: Filing dated 'Friday' (most likely Nov 13); first reported Nov 15–16. Prosecutors also asked that Pannun be allowed to speak for 20 minutes at sentencing. Related watch: W-261114-09.

items.text: Stars and Stripes reports that about 78,000 US personnel were assigned to European Command at the end of September, near the 76,000 floor set in the FY2026 NDAA. Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby has reportedly delivered force-posture findings to Defense Secretary Hegseth. Citing Bloomberg, it says final cuts could be as small as 5,000 troops, mostly from Germany, while the eastern flank could see more US presence. It recalls that a planned armoured brigade rotation to Poland was cancelled in May.
items.notes: Bloomberg's 5,000-cut figure may already be logged under US. Nothing found on Colby at the EU defence ministerial (W-261114-08). Related watches: W-261108-11 and W-261111-05.
